valid_fixes: Remove the RedrivePolicy from InventoryUpdatesDlq entirely so the DLQ does not redirect messages back to the main queue
Restore SQSToDynamoDBFunction.Environment.Variables.DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME to !Ref InventoryUpdatesTable to stop consumer failures that trigger the loop
invalid_patches: Set InventoryUpdatesDlq.RedrivePolicy.maxReceiveCount to a higher value — does not break the loop, only delays it
Fix only the DLQ circular redrive without fixing the wrong table name — consumer still fails, messages cycle indefinitely through main queue and DLQ
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_get_log_tail(function=SQSToDynamoDBFunction) → repeated ResourceNotFoundException for inventory-staging table — wrong table name in env var
ace_check_queue_depth(queue=InventoryUpdatesDlq) → DLQ shows messages transiently then drops to 0 — messages leaving DLQ without a consumer
ace_describe_resource(resource=InventoryUpdatesDlq) → DLQ has RedrivePolicy pointing back to main queue — confirms circular loop
observable_symptom: The consumer is invoked and logs show repeated ResourceNotFoundException for a non-existent table. Messages appear in the dead-letter queue after exhausting retries, then disappear and reappear in the main queue. Neither queue reaches a stable state. No records are written to the database.
root_cause: Two faults combine: (1) DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME points to a non-existent inventory-staging table, causing every consumer invocation to fail with ResourceNotFoundException; (2) InventoryUpdatesDlq is given a RedrivePolicy that routes messages back to InventoryUpdatesQueue with maxReceiveCount=1. After 5 failures on the main queue, messages move to the DLQ. After 1 receive on the DLQ (with no consumer), they cycle back to the main queue — creating an infinite bounce loop. Neither fault alone produces this pattern.
